question: Can source-visible overlap or text sequence establish which Fr 8994 partial photographs share a surface, without assuming photograph ordinals are medieval sides?
prior_inspection: E33 has already inspected incipits in photos 1,3,4; this follow-up is exploratory and not blind. Protocol precedes the new overlap inspection.
hypothesis: Photo pairs 1/2 and 3/4 show complementary parts of two surfaces. This is a hypothesis, not an assigned side map.
alternatives: Nonoverlapping portions of the same surface
Parts from opposite surfaces or more than one leaf
Repeated chant text without identical photographed detail
Order/signature convention differs from presumed side order

predictions.repeated_photographed_detail: Overlapping writing strokes, damage and ruling can establish shared photographed material. Text identity alone is weaker.
predictions.text_only: Consecutive text can support relative reading order but cannot prove same surface or a physical join.
predictions.absence: No overlap or failed registration cannot establish different surfaces.

test: Inspect all four originals; record exact regions/literal candidates before consulting further concordances. If an overlap is visible, test fixed image correspondences against another-pair control; otherwise report incomplete mapping.
constraints: No new downloads, editing, automatic side assignment or alteration of frozen reviews.
